dedupe_keys.name: nees bncs full scale five storey building shake table and post earthquake fire test gps displacement data

description: This NEES dataset records displacements measured by collocated GPS and accelerometer sensor packages during the BNCS landmark test, in which a full-scale five-storey building with a complete set of nonstructural components was shaken on the outdoor shake table at UC San Diego and then subjected to post-earthquake fire tests. It was collected by the Scripps Institution of Oceanography (Yehuda Bock, Diego Melgar) and the Department of Structural Engineering (José Restrepo, Elide Pantoli) and published through the Network for Earthquake Engineering Simulation in 2013; the project was funded by the National Science Foundation (CMMI 0936505). The building contained a working passenger elevator, partition walls, cladding and glazing, piping, ceilings, sprinklers, contents and passive and active fire systems, making it a rare test of how building services perform in earthquakes, relevant to hospitals and other critical facilities. Coverage: one test building, from five sensor packages. Access: open download from the DesignSafe Data Depot. Licence: not stated in the DataCite record; free. Caveats: GPS data are one part of a large project; other sensor data sit in related NEES experiments. Simulation uses are validation of structural and nonstructural response models and of GPS-based structural monitoring. Related records: the EPFL mixed RC and masonry shake table data.
